Alexander Hale

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 7, Harris County, Texas · Challenger

Management consultant (Senior Associate, Alvarez & Marsal)

Alexander Hale is a Houston management consultant who works with companies in the energy and chemicals sectors. Ballotpedia describes him as an energy and chemicals consultant. He advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for Texas' 7th Congressional District to a runoff and defeated Tina Blum Cohen in the May 26, 2026 runoff to become the Republican nominee.

Where Hale stands

Education
Says every TX-07 child deserves access to a quality education and supports school choice and innovative approaches to improve student results.
Public safety
Supports backing local authorities and law enforcement and opposes what he calls soft-on-crime policies. Proposes addressing crime affecting Houston neighborhoods.
Federal spending and debt
Supports cutting wasteful spending and ending government programs he considers ineffective. Says he will offer honest analysis of the national debt.
Energy
Lists protecting the district's energy economy as a local priority.
Border security
Lists securing the border as a priority for the district.
Infrastructure (power grid and water)
Calls managing Texas' growth while keeping infrastructure reliable the state's greatest challenge. Supports major investment in power grid reliability and water security.
Government accountability
Proposes eliminating what he describes as systematic fraud in federally funded NGOs and public assistance programs.
Constituent services
Pledges to hold town halls and keep a visible presence across the Harris and Fort Bend County parts of the district.

Background

  • Senior Associate, Alvarez & Marsal (2022–present)
  • Previously worked at WoodRock & Co. (per BallotReady)
  • Bachelor's degree, Baylor University
  • Fourth-generation Houstonian; lives in the Heights
  • Won 2026 Republican primary runoff for U.S. House TX-07 (May 26, 2026)
  • No prior elected office found

Also running for U.S. Representative, District 7

  • Lizzie Pannill Fletcher Democratic
  • Espoir Ngabo Green
